pr.title: Emit dummy open drop for unsafe binder
pr.description:
Fixes rust-lang/rust#141394

We can't taint the body in wfcheck when we have a `T: Copy` bound failure, so we end up binding MIR here. Emit a dummy open drop so that drop elaboration doesn't fail.

r? oli-obk

issues.title: ICE: `open drop from non-ADT` with `unsafe_binder`

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: open drop for unsafe binder shouldn't be encountered
use crate::elaborate_drop::{DropElaborator, DropFlagMode, DropStyle, Unwind, elaborate_drop};

The patch adds an `UnsafeBinder` arm to `DropCtxt::open_drop` in compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elaborate_drop.rs. Inspected historical source confirms this module backs the concrete `ElaborateDrops` MirPass in elaborate_drops.rs, whose `run_pass` invokes drop elaboration. This prevents an ICE during MIR drop elaboration by emitting a dummy unreachable block, so it is a drop-elaboration correctness change, not cleanup.

processing.reason: The PR is an ICE fix, not a value-level miscompilation. Its historical "wrong transformation" is that `DropCtxt::open_drop` had no `ty::UnsafeBinder(_)` arm, so a binder type fell through to the catch-all `span_bug!("open drop from non-ADT ...")`, aborting compilation. The correction adds an arm that reports a delayed bug and emits a dummy `TerminatorKind::Unreachable` block. Neither revision produces a defined successful return value for the matched `unsafe<> T`/non-Copy input: the old path panics/aborts the compiler, and the corrected path builds an unreachable CFG block after a diagnostic. Encoding this as two value-returning Rust functions would require inventing a panic-vs-sentinel or arbitrary return-value difference not present in the historical transformation, which the task forbids. Additionally, the triggering input depends on the unstable `#![feature(unsafe_binders)]` and internal MIR drop-elaboration state, which cannot be faithfully exercised as an ordinary fixed-compiler/Miri runtime program. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair with differing defined Miri results exists.

analysis.summary: ElaborateDrops ICE when drop elaboration encountered an `unsafe<> T` (`ty::UnsafeBinder`) open drop whose inner type was not Copy. The fix adds an UnsafeBinder arm to `DropCtxt::open_drop` that reports a delayed bug and emits a dummy unreachable block so drop elaboration completes; a UI regression test checks only E0277 is produced (no ICE) under `-Zvalidate-mir`.
analysis.originalLogic: In `DropCtxt::open_drop`, the compiler matched `ty.kind()` and handled structured types (ADT, tuple, array, slice, etc.), with a catch-all `_ => span_bug!(self.source_info.span, "open drop from non-ADT `{:?}`", ty)`. There was no `ty::UnsafeBinder` arm, so a binder type reaching open-drop fell into that catch-all panic.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, when MIR drop elaboration encountered an open drop for `ty::UnsafeBinder(_)` (e.g. `unsafe<> T` with non-Copy `T`), the compiler treated it as an unhandled non-ADT and routed it to the `span_bug!` catch-all, aborting compilation with an ICE (`open drop from non-ADT `Binder { value: T/#0, bound_vars: [] }``). The corrected transformation instead matches `ty::UnsafeBinder(_)`, emits a `span_delayed_bug` with `"open drop for unsafe binder shouldn't be encountered"`, and creates a new block containing no statements, `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`, the current `source_info`, and `is_cleanup: self.unwind.is_cleanup()`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source programs using the unstable `#![feature(unsafe_binders)]` (and `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`), specifically functions taking an `unsafe<> T` parameter where `T` is generic and not `Copy`, with a body that moves out via `std::unsafe_binder::unwrap_binder!(x)`. These are compiled through MIR with the `ElaborateDrops` pass; the regression test also passes `-Zvalidate-mir`. The path can be reached despite a WF/typeck `E0277` because the body is still bound for MIR.
analysis.trigger: Drop elaboration reaches `DropCtxt::open_drop` for a value whose type is `ty::UnsafeBinder(_)`, which happens when a function has an `unsafe<> T` parameter with a non-Copy `T` and moves out of it.
preconditions: A function parameter has binder type `unsafe<> T` where `T` is generic and does not satisfy `Copy`.
The body moves out of the binder (e.g. `unwrap_binder!(x)`), so drop elaboration considers the binder type.
Typeck/wfcheck may report E0277 for `T: Copy`, but that does not taint the body and MIR is still bound with the UnsafeBinder type.
The `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass runs over the body (the regression test additionally uses `-Zvalidate-mir`).
pitfalls: Do not assume a WF/typeck error (E0277) prevents MIR binding or drop elaboration; the binder type still reaches `open_drop`.
Do not route `ty::UnsafeBinder(_)` through the generic non-ADT `span_bug!` path; that is precisely the ICE.
The recovery block must be constructed consistently: empty statements, `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`, correct `source_info`, and `is_cleanup` derived from `self.unwind.is_cleanup()`.
Keep `span_delayed_bug` rather than silently swallowing the situation, so internal diagnostics are preserved while the expected user-facing E0277 remains the only error.
An identical ICE location can arise from different features/bisects (issue notes #140930 at the same location), so tests must specifically use unsafe binders.
A `Copy`-constrained binder may avoid the open-drop path, so the regression test must use an unconstrained/non-Copy `T` to trigger it.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test `tests/ui/unsafe/move-out-of-non-copy.rs` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zvalidate-mir`, enabling `#![feature(unsafe_binders)]` and `#![allow(incomplete_features)]`. Define `fn id<T>(x: unsafe<> T) -> T { unsafe { unwrap_binder!(x) } }` and annotate the `unsafe<> T` parameter with the expected E0277 (`the trait bound `T: Copy` is not satisfied`). The `.stderr` expectation must contain only that E0277 and the “aborting due to 1 previous error” line, and must not contain an ICE or `open drop from non-ADT`. This exercises MIR drop elaboration on the UnsafeBinder open-drop path.
evidence: We can't taint the body in wfcheck when we have a `T: Copy` bound failure, so we end up binding MIR here. Emit a dummy open drop so that drop elaboration doesn't fail.
